verdict_text: NO. The script does not write `out/T4/model.safetensors` per the task's fixed output path; it accepts a CLI arg defaulting to `out/T4`, but if invoked without exactly matching that default (or as documented in TASK.md, run via `python out/<task>/solution.py` with no args) it still works, so this itself is not the violation. The real violation: it uses bare `assert` statements for all required checks (shared-tensor verification, tensor-name matching outside MLP set, merged count, output count), which are stripped out when Python is run with `-O`, silently disabling every one of the "Required checks" the spec mandates must "fail loudly" — this is not a robust, loud failure mechanism as required. Additionally, the shared-tensor check only verifies non-MLP tensors are equal but never checks that the *set of MLP tensor names* matches the spec's expected 64 (it relies on regex matching against `base`'s keys only, trusting `ft1`/`ft2` have the same keys via the earlier `set` equality, which is fine) — so this part is actually acceptable. The dispositive flaw is the reliance on `assert` for all required-check failures, violating the "fail loudly" requirement in Required checks.
